archetype.name: Cup Contender (5-on-5 possession)
archetype.definition: A team that owns the puck and the chances at even strength well enough to sit near the top of the league, even with special teams and goaltending that are only ordinary so far.

report.headline: Elite at 5-on-5, leaky on special teams: the record is earned
report.take:
Tampa Bay is 15-6-2, fourth on the site, and the record rests on something solid. At 5-on-5 the Lightning take a 56.6% share of the expected goals and 55% of the shot attempts, both third in the league, and they allow only 25 shots a game. That xGF % is the best in any of their last five seasons, including the 106-point team of a year ago. The Goal Diff / GP of 0.7 (sixth) is not a close-game mirage either: Pts vs Goal Diff sits at a modest 1.6, so the standings mostly match the margins.

The engine is the top of the forward group. Nikita Kucherov has 32 points in 23 games with a 60.7% xGF share, Brayden Point has 18, and the forwards grade out A-. Behind them the depth is thin: the listed bottom-six wingers have two points each. The blueline (C+) is defined by Erik Cernak's +11 and 60.4% xGF beside J.J. Moser's one point in 23 games. Tampa's defense also gives up an unusually large share of its points against to opposing defensemen.

What the numbers hide is a split between even strength and special teams. The 5-on-5 PDO of 101.8 says Tampa has gotten some bounces at even strength. The all-situations PDO of 99.1 sits at about league average, though, because the PK (73.3%, 23rd) and PP (21.3%, 19th) are bleeding value. The PK has been between 79.7% and 83.3% in each of the last five seasons, so it should recover. The power play was also mediocre last year at 20.7%, so that weakness looks more lasting. Goaltending, historically Tampa's trump card, is merely average: team GSAx of -0.3 against 12.5 last year and 26.9 the year before.

The direction is good. Goals against fell from 3.31 a game in October to 2.5 in November while scoring held near 3.6. Even so, the last five games cooled to 2.6 goals a game, with a shutout loss to Detroit and a 6-2 home loss to Buffalo. A full 82-game pace of 114 points overstates things slightly once the 5-on-5 bounces even out. A PK regression in Tampa's favor and any return to form from Vasilevskiy would cover that gap.

strengths.title: Controls play at 5-on-5
strengths.body: Tampa ranks third in both xGF % and CF %, and it limits volume at the other end. This is a structural edge, not a hot streak: it is a step up even on last season's 54% xGF, and possession numbers are the stickiest in hockey. Expect it to last.

strengths.title: Kucherov-Point top line drives everything
strengths.body: Kucherov's 32 points and 60.7% xGF share make him the second-ranked right wing on the site, and Point is fourth among centers. Both are winning their minutes on chances, not just converting, so the production is well supported. The risk is concentration: if either misses time, the depth behind them has not shown it can carry scoring.

strengths.title: Defense tightening as the season goes
strengths.body: Goals against dropped from October to November while the scoring rate barely moved, which is why the last 10 went 7-3 with a strong margin. This fits the shot suppression underneath it, so it should mostly hold.

concerns.title: Penalty kill well below the league
concerns.body: At 73.3%, the PK is 23rd and well below the league average. It is the main reason Tampa's all-situations PDO is ordinary despite strong 5-on-5 results. Every recent Tampa team killed penalties at 79.7% or better, so some of this is noise likely to correct. Until it does, it is costing a goal here and there in tight games.

concerns.title: Goaltending is average, not elite
concerns.body: Team GSAx is -0.3 (17th). Vasilevskiy is modestly positive at 2.0, and Hildeby is at -1.5 over six starts. A franchise that posted double-digit GSAx in three of the last four years is now winning without a goaltending edge. That is a weakness only relative to the past, and it gives the team upside if the starter finds his old level.

concerns.title: Opposing defensemen feast; own D quiet
concerns.body: Tampa ranks 23rd at holding opposing defensemen under their norms. Defensemen account for 40% of the points against, far above the league's share, which points to point shots and activations getting through. Its own blueline gives little back: Moser has one point in 23 games, and the group grades C+.

trend.note: Goals against dropped sharply from October to November and the last 10 went 7-3. The last five cooled offensively, at 2.6 goals a game with two lopsided losses mixed in.

weekAhead.headline: The league's best, a division rival, then a back-to-back
weekAhead.body:
The week opens at home against Carolina, the site's No. 1 team at 18-3-3. The Hurricanes are the one opponent that beats Tampa at its own game: first in xGF % (60.6%), first in CF %, first in shots allowed, and first at holding forwards under their norms. Their 105.9 all-situations PDO is inflated by a 16.1% shooting rate that should cool, but not necessarily this week. A split of the possession battle would be a good night.

Ottawa comes in on Friday tied with Tampa atop the Atlantic but sitting 16th on the site. The Senators lead the league in Pts vs Goal Diff, have the worst power play in the league, and give up the most production to wingers of anyone on the slate, a clean setup for Kucherov. The next night at Florida is the second half of a back-to-back. The Panthers' wingers are stifled but centers produce against them (28th), they kill penalties at 84.6%, and their forwards grade F. Two of the three games are winnable, and Tampa is the better 5-on-5 team in both.

keyMatchups.title: Tampa's possession vs Carolina's wall
keyMatchups.body: Carolina allows the fewest shots in the league and holds opposing forwards furthest under expectation. That is a direct test of whether Kucherov and Point can still drive play against the one team with better underlying numbers.

keyMatchups.title: Ottawa's luck and leaky wing coverage
keyMatchups.body: Ottawa's standings outrun its goal margin more than any team's, and it ranks 26th against wingers. Tampa's special-teams weakness matters less against a 13.5% power play.

keyMatchups.title: Point's lane in Florida
keyMatchups.body: Florida allows centers to beat their norms (28th) while choking off wingers (3rd), so the second night of the back-to-back may run through Point rather than Kucherov. Florida's strong PK also means even strength will decide it.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Tampa's penalty kill holds up against Carolina's power play, which converts at 25.6%. A bad night there is how the Lightning lose a game they otherwise compete in.

restOfSeason.body:
The 5-on-5 dominance is the most durable thing on this sheet, so Tampa should stay among the Atlantic's top teams. The 5-on-5 PDO above 100 will likely fade somewhat. The penalty kill is the obvious candidate to improve given the franchise's track record, and the two should roughly offset. Goaltending is the swing: average so far, with real upside if Vasilevskiy trends back toward past seasons.

The 114-point pace is the ceiling scenario. A more realistic band is around 104 to 112 points, scoring holding near current levels, and a division race that stays crowded with Ottawa, Boston and Montreal all close in the standings.
swingFactors: Penalty kill recovering toward its usual level
Health of the Kucherov-Point top line

confidence.note: 23 games is a small sample, but strong possession numbers back the record.
